newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU sees continued heavy reliance on oil imports.
newsitem.headline: EU sees continued heavy reliance on oil imports.

text.p: European Union energy ministers said on Tuesday that the Union would continue to depend heavily on imported oil, adding that "there is an ongoing need for vigilance in both the short and long term."
The Energy Council agreed on Council Conclusions on a report by the European Commission on the situation of oil supply, refining and markets in the EU.
"More than three quarters of proven world oil reserves are located in potentially sensitive areas," the conclusions said.

"This highlights the continuing requirement to maintain existing measures such as stockholding procedures and crisis management mechanisms, which may be adapted where necessary to changing market circumstances," they added.
The ministers also said that to the extent that rationalisation occurs, including refinery closures as a last resort, individual companies must remain responsible for decisions about capacity.
But they noted that "regard is given to the requirement of member states in relation to security of supply."
They said a healthy refining sector "underpins economic and social progress" in the EU, provides security of supply and is capable of supporting environmental protection measures.
The ministers also said the Commission's report had identified some of the main causes of the current difficulties in the sector such as excess refining capacity in the EU.
They recommended that that the causes should be subject to further detailed studies and asked the Commission to undertake these studies and to continue to monitor and analyse the situation.
